Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The Season 14 Shield Charge Thorns Paladin read forward onto the 3.2.0 PTR, and the quietest of the five carried builds. 3.2.0 gives Paladin the +30% core stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) and adjusts the Holy line - Holy Bolt, Blessed Shield, and a redesigned Judgement - but the digest's summary is 'surprisingly few changes' overall, and set balance is explicitly still unaddressed. None of the Holy-line changes touch this build: Shield Charge, Clash, Condemn, Fortress and the two auras are not mentioned in the 3.2.0 notes, and neither is Resolve or Retribution. So the loop below is intact, the Resolve-30 arithmetic is intact, and the scalar is a straight gain on a build whose damage is Physical Thorns scaled through Resolve. That is the good news and it is genuinely modest: both 3.2.0 class tier reads keep Paladin at B, exactly where TierListHQ had it in Season 14, so a +30% baseline buff has not moved the class in the eyes of the only sources that exist. The Season 14 reading still applies - this is the strongest solo Paladin build available rather than a top-of-meta build, its only S-tier company anywhere is a group-only support build, and its cons are structural: short range and a hard positioning requirement that Pit boss floors punish. Season 14 data read forward; 3.2.0 publishes no build guides, skill allocations or paragon orderings for any class.

Rotation
  1. Open with Condemn to pull the pack together, keep Clash refreshed at least every six seconds, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle so the blocks pulse Retribution.
  2. Save Fortress for when you are surrounded or on a boss, and pre-gather with Condemn before every charge pass.
Variants

Leveling — Open with Condemn to pull the pack together, keep Clash refreshed, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle of the group so the blocks pulse Retribution. Drop Fortress when you are surrounded or on a boss for the immunity and damage window, and use Defiance Aura's active to break crowd control.
Move on when Mantle of the Grey in the chest and Herald of Zakarum in the shield slot - the guide's own difference between Starter and Midgame - with Tibault's Will following.

Early Endgame — Identical to the previous stage: Condemn to gather, Clash at least every six seconds, Shield Charge as the spam through the middle of the pack, Fortress for immunity and its Resolve damage bonus.
Move on when The three uniques equipped and the Resolve tempering chase underway - at which point the build stops being about acquisition and starts being about hitting two hard caps.

Late Endgame — Unchanged from the early endgame. This stage is a tempering and masterworking project, not a gameplay change - which is worth saying plainly, because a build page that implies a new rotation at every stage is lying about what the guide actually publishes.
Move on when Resolve at 30 with Block and Critical Strike Chance capped on masterworked gear. Then swap to the push variant's Mythic and charm-set layout.

Pushing — The same loop, played more carefully. Fortress becomes a planned cooldown for dangerous floors rather than a free button, and you pre-gather with Condemn before every Shield Charge pass - because the guide's two cons, short range and required positioning, bite hardest exactly here.

Stat requirements
  • [ptr] Reach the Resolve cap of 30
Lootfilter

Shield Charge Paladin — Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The guide ships three strictness tiers as import codes in its Loot Filter section; those are the exact match and its own caveat is that 'these provide a baseline you can adjust to your own liking'. The community sites were checked: the Paladin filters surfaced on diablo4lootfilter.com appear to be Season 13 and none is Shield-Charge-specific, so none is linked here rather than a stale mismatch being presented as an alternative.

Uniques
  • chest [ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: Target-farm Harbinger of Hatred. Crafting priority #1 in every variant - it is one of the three things Resolve scales your damage through, alongside the Juggernaut Oath and the Sentinel glyph. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch. Where →
  • offhand [ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: Target-farm Astaroth. The build's shield, and last on the Mythic crafting order because the other three do more for you first. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch. Where →
  • pants [ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so any boss can drop it and the reliable route is the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. Crafting priority #2. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: Push variant only, where it slots in at crafting priority #2 ahead of Tibault's Will. General Unique Pool - any boss encounter - or the Horadric Cube. Remember the standing rule the guide restates: you can equip only one Mythic crafted in the Horadric Cube, but any number acquired elsewhere. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Skill point priority

  1. Scope note: this is an endgame-only guide - it 'assumes you have a Level 70 Character and unlocked Torment 1' and links three separate Paladin levelling guides - so this stage records its Starter variant rather than a 1-70 route it never published
  2. Shield Charge is the main damage: always position to hit the most enemies so Hit Count As Blocking triggers as often as possible
  3. Clash keeps its buff up - one cast per six seconds minimum - and is your Retribution chance, Thorns and Block Chance
  4. Fanaticism Aura ranks: 14% critical strike chance at 15 ranks, and the source of Vulnerable, Weaken and Fortify
  5. Defiance Aura ranks for health recovery and Resolve generation, and it can be activated for Unstoppable
  6. Fortress for the three-second immunity plus its Resolve damage bonus; Condemn for grouping and Unhindered

Skill point priority

  1. Reach the Resolve cap of 30, and know the arithmetic: 'your basline maximum Resolve is 8 and you need 3x +6 Maximum Resolve Tempers, Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the Phoba of Righteous Will set to reach exactly 30 Maximum Resolve'. The temper needs to crit and then Masterwork-crit to reach +6
  2. Cap Block Chance through Aegis at rank 15, the Castle and Shield Bearer boards, Aspect of Interdiction and Bulwark's Aspect
  3. Cap Critical Strike Chance through Fanaticism Aura ranks, charm and seal affixes, weapon tempers and Masterwork focus
  4. Then, and only then, chase Critical Strike Damage: 'the value of Critical Strike Damage multiplier goes up as you can acquire more Critical Strike Chance. If you have very low Critical Strike Chance, Physical Damage, Vulnerable Damage or All Damage multipliers have more value'
  5. Defensively, 'focus on Armor and Maximum Life and the Aspects provided in the planner'

How to run them

[ptr] Carried over from Season 14 unchanged: the official 3.2.0 notes do not mention mercenaries at all. Identical across all four variants: hire Raheir, who 'grants you Bastion and Inspiration to buff your damage', and reinforce with Aldkin, who 'reduces enemy damage and slows with Field of Languish'. Note this is the opposite emphasis from most Season 14 builds, which take Raheir purely for survivability - here Inspiration is picked up as a damage node, which is the tell that this build already has its own defence covered by block, Resolve and Fortress and is spending the mercenary slot on offence and on the damage-reduction layer instead.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The Season 14 Shield Charge Thorns Paladin read forward onto the 3.2.0 PTR, and the quietest of the five carried builds. 3.2.0 gives Paladin the +30% core stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) and adjusts the Holy line - Holy Bolt, Blessed Shield, and a redesigned Judgement - but the digest's summary is 'surprisingly few changes' overall, and set balance is explicitly still unaddressed. None of the Holy-line changes touch this build: Shield Charge, Clash, Condemn, Fortress and the two auras are not mentioned in the 3.2.0 notes, and neither is Resolve or Retribution. So the loop below is intact, the Resolve-30 arithmetic is intact, and the scalar is a straight gain on a build whose damage is Physical Thorns scaled through Resolve. That is the good news and it is genuinely modest: both 3.2.0 class tier reads keep Paladin at B, exactly where TierListHQ had it in Season 14, so a +30% baseline buff has not moved the class in the eyes of the only sources that exist. The Season 14 reading still applies - this is the strongest solo Paladin build available rather than a top-of-meta build, its only S-tier company anywhere is a group-only support build, and its cons are structural: short range and a hard positioning requirement that Pit boss floors punish. Season 14 data read forward; 3.2.0 publishes no build guides, skill allocations or paragon orderings for any class.

Rotation
  1. Open with Condemn to pull the pack together, keep Clash refreshed at least every six seconds, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle so the blocks pulse Retribution.
  2. Save Fortress for when you are surrounded or on a boss, and pre-gather with Condemn before every charge pass.
Variants

Leveling — Open with Condemn to pull the pack together, keep Clash refreshed, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle of the group so the blocks pulse Retribution. Drop Fortress when you are surrounded or on a boss for the immunity and damage window, and use Defiance Aura's active to break crowd control.
Move on when Mantle of the Grey in the chest and Herald of Zakarum in the shield slot - the guide's own difference between Starter and Midgame - with Tibault's Will following.

Early Endgame — Identical to the previous stage: Condemn to gather, Clash at least every six seconds, Shield Charge as the spam through the middle of the pack, Fortress for immunity and its Resolve damage bonus.
Move on when The three uniques equipped and the Resolve tempering chase underway - at which point the build stops being about acquisition and starts being about hitting two hard caps.

Late Endgame — Unchanged from the early endgame. This stage is a tempering and masterworking project, not a gameplay change - which is worth saying plainly, because a build page that implies a new rotation at every stage is lying about what the guide actually publishes.
Move on when Resolve at 30 with Block and Critical Strike Chance capped on masterworked gear. Then swap to the push variant's Mythic and charm-set layout.

Pushing — The same loop, played more carefully. Fortress becomes a planned cooldown for dangerous floors rather than a free button, and you pre-gather with Condemn before every Shield Charge pass - because the guide's two cons, short range and required positioning, bite hardest exactly here.

Stat requirements
  • [ptr] Reach the Resolve cap of 30

The build's shield, and last on the Mythic crafting order because the other three do more for you first. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch. Where →

Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so any boss can drop it and the reliable route is the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. Crafting priority #2. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: Push variant only, where it slots in at crafting priority #2 ahead of Tibault's Will. General Unique Pool - any boss encounter - or the Horadric Cube. Remember the standing rule the guide restates: you can equip only one Mythic crafted in the Horadric Cube, but any number acquired elsewhere. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Provoke

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Raheir Taunts enemies around you for 5 seconds. You gain 5% Damage Reduction for each target, up to 20%.

Ground Slam

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Round Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Strike

Raheir brutalizes the ground, dealing 160% Physical damage and Slowing enemies by 30% for 6 seconds. Targets in the center of the slam are Slowed by 60% instead.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir swings a round shield at enemies, dealing 85% Physical damage. Every 20 swings, Raheir Heals you for 8% of your Maximum Life.

Shield Charge

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Tower Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Bash

Raheir rushes forward aggressively, dealing 110% Physical damage and Taunting nearby enemies for 4 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir bashes enemies with a tower shield, dealing 80% Physical damage and Fortifying you for 0.2% of your Maximum Life.

Crater

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir strikes the ground 3 times, each burst dealing 30% Physical damage and Pulling In enemies. The final burst deals 40% more Physical damage and additionally Stuns enemies for 2 seconds.

Raheir's Guard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15%[+] Armor.

Vanguard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir Slows surrounding enemies by 40%.

Mocking Lure

PassiveRaheir

You deal 15%[x] increased damage to enemies Taunted by Raheir.

Iron Wolf's Ward

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Knocks Back Close enemies and Taunts Distant enemies for 4 seconds.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Iron Wolf's Call

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, your next 4 Core Skills within 10 seconds deal 25%[x] increased damage and cost no Resource.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 25%.

Sundering Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's final Crater burst deals 200%[x] increased damage and inflicts Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Shield Throw

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir throws his shield, dealing 450% Physical damage and Taunting enemies for 5 seconds. The shield bounces up to 9 times and cannot bounce to the same target twice.

Iron Wolf's Arrival

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he also casts Ground Slam and Shield Throw.

Raheir's Valiance's Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Consecrated Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's Shield Throw Consecrates enemies for 6 seconds. Directly damaging a Consecrated enemy Heals you for 6% of your Maximum Life, once per target.

Bastion

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 30 seconds

Raheir takes a protective position for 5 seconds, redirecting 90% of the damage that would be dealt to surrounding allies to himself for 5 seconds.

Bastion's initial cast also grants surrounding allies Unstoppable for 1.0 seconds.

Iron Wolf's Virtue

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Heals you for 25% of your Maximum Life.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Inspiration

PassiveRaheir

Enemies affected by Raheir's Ground Slam take 15%[x] increased damage.

Allies affected by Raheir's Bastion deal 25%[x] increased damage.

Raheir's Aegis

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15% Resistance to All Elements.

Draw Fire

PassiveRaheir

When you use a Healing Potion, Raheir Taunts enemies around him for 4 seconds. Can only occur once every 20 seconds.
